494	## Project Milestone — milestone-as-Epic via `parent`, label fallback
495	
496	Jira opts into project-milestone binding (`project_milestone: true` in the
497	frontmatter). Jira has no per-issue "milestone" field on the standard MCP
498	surface, but it does have a native container: the **Epic**. The primary
499	binding (`milestone_binding: epic` in the frontmatter) realises each
500	milestone as an Epic issue created under its human title, from whose
501	tracker-assigned key the milestone id is derived; the
502	FR Task binds by pointing its `parent` field at that Epic's key. When the
503	bound project has no Epic type (or cannot set `parent`), the binding
504	degrades to the legacy **label** path documented further down — never a
505	hard failure.
506	
507	### Epic path (primary — `milestone_binding: epic`)
508	
509	**Find.** Enumerate the project's Epics via
510	`mcp__atlassian__searchJiraIssuesUsingJql` with
511	`jql = "project = <projectKey> AND issuetype = Epic"` and match the milestone's
512	Epic by KEY when the plan heading carries an `M_<key>` token: sanitize each
513	candidate's key forward (`GF-78` → `M_GF_78`) and compare. For an Epic-KEYED
514	milestone, summary equality is not the join — the canonical name embeds the
515	very key being looked for, while the Epic itself carries the human title typed
516	at creation. A name that carries NO token — a pre-key human title, the state
517	between minting the Epic and writing the plan file — has no key to compare, so
518	that one arm still matches by NAME, byte-exactly. Both arms refuse on a miss:
519	binding never creates.
520	
521	**Mint — create, read the key back, derive the id, then write the plan file.**
522	A milestone Epic is minted in the only order whose values exist at the moment
523	each is needed. `adapters/_shared/src/mint_milestone_epic.ts` performs steps
524	1–3; its caller performs step 4. Step 1 is wrapped in a find-before-create
525	retry on the canonical `1s + 2s + 4s` schedule: a create that lands in Jira and
526	then times out is FOUND on the retry and reused, never created a second time.
527	That protection is why a timeout does not mint a duplicate Epic.
528	
529	1. Create the Epic with the **human title alone** —
530	   `mcp__atlassian__createJiraIssue(projectKey=<projectKey>,
531	   issueTypeName="Epic", summary=<human title>)`. The canonical
532	   `M_<key> — <Title>` name is not available here: it embeds the key Jira is
533	   about to allocate for this very Epic, so ordering it would order a value
534	   that does not yet exist.
535	2. **read the key back** from the create response, verbatim (`GF-78`).
536	3. **derive the id** from that key via `milestoneIdFromEpicKey` (`GF-78` →
537	   `M_GF_78`); a key that will not sanitize into a well-formed id refuses
538	   rather than yielding a malformed one.
539	4. **write the plan file** under that id, with heading `## M_<key> — <Title>`.
540	
541	**Epic label — at mint time only.** After it derives the id, and outside the
542	step-1 retry, the mint writes the label `milestone-M_<key>` on the Epic itself
543	(`milestone-M_GF_78` for `GF-78`). That label is a read-side convenience: it
544	lets a repo enumerating a shared project find the milestone by its label. It
545	is never the binding surface — membership stays the FR's `parent`, below. A
546	failed label write never fails the mint: the Epic and its derived id stand,
547	and only the convenience is missing. In a live session the write is a
548	read-merge-write on the Epic's own key —
549	`mcp__atlassian__editJiraIssue(issueIdOrKey=<epic-key>,
550	additional_fields={ labels: [...<existing labels>, "milestone-M_<key>"] })`,
551	never clobbering a label already there. `mintMilestoneEpic` performs it
552	through the provider's `addLabel` and reports whether it landed as
553	`labelled`; its command form prints the label it would write as
554	`label=milestone-M_<key>` beside the derived id.
555	
556	**Joining, never minting.** A repo joining a container another repo already
557	minted calls the mint with `{ join: true }`. Its find leg compares titles
558	after normalizing whitespace and case: exactly one match joins that Epic, two
559	or more refuse and name every candidate with its key, and no match — or a
560	provider carrying no `listEpics` — refuses instead of creating. A join never
561	creates. The toolkit makes every other mint with the approved decision of
562	`resolve_milestone_identity.ts` as `expect`, so it performs that act or refuses; only a bare mint with neither option still finds by title.
563	
564	The mint surfaces NO capability row: it is a step of its own, not an attach
565	outcome, and the attach that follows FINDS the Epic and returns `capability:
566	null`. `milestone_create_required` belongs to the object binding's
567	`save_milestone` auto-create, which this path never reaches.
568	
569	**Membership — `parent` set.** Bind the FR Task by writing the Epic's key to
570	its `parent` field: `mcp__atlassian__editJiraIssue(issueIdOrKey=ticket_id,
571	additional_fields={ parent: { key: <epic-key> } })`. This path never touches
572	milestone objects. For an Epic-KEYED milestone the per-FR attach writes no
573	`milestone-<M-token>` label on the FR ticket; the only `milestone-M_<key>`
574	label such a milestone carries is the one the mint writes on the Epic itself.
575	A grandfathered NUMERIC `M<N>` milestone under this same binding deliberately
576	DOES take the label surface on the ticket, because that is where the reader's
577	own grandfather clause looks for it; see the numeric note below.
578	Idempotency pre-check: the issue is read FIRST, before any Epic is listed
579	(STE-611). When its binding is already present the attach is a no-op, with
580	no enumeration and no write, even when that parent Epic lives in another
581	project (a legacy `GB-40` parent under a repository now bound to `GF`).
582	
583	**Read-back verify.** Re-read the issue (`getJiraIssue`) and assert
584	`parent = <epic-key>`. A mismatch surfaces the canonical binding-mismatch
585	error (never retried); transient failures retry the whole round-trip on the
586	canonical `1s + 2s + 4s` schedule.
587	
588	**Grandfathered numeric milestones — the numeric note.** A project that adopts
589	Epic-keyed milestones still has its old numeric `M<N>` ones. Under this same
590	`milestone_binding: epic`, a numeric token does NOT bind by parent Epic: it
591	takes the `milestone-M<N>` LABEL surface, through the same read-merge-write
592	attach the legacy binding uses. That is not an inconsistency — it is the only
593	arrangement that converges, because the reader's own grandfather clause looks
594	for a numeric milestone on the label surface. Binding by parent while the
595	reader checks labels is what made a backfill sweep report the same work done on
596	every pass forever. There is nothing to configure: the routing is decided by
597	the milestone TOKEN's kind, not by the adapter's declared binding.
598	
599	**Epic-absent fallback.** Probe the bound project's issue-type metadata via
600	`mcp__atlassian__getJiraProjectIssueTypesMetadata`. When the Epic type is
601	absent — or the project cannot set `parent` — the attach degrades to the
602	label path below and the closing summary surfaces the **informational**
603	`milestone_epic_unsupported` capability row (the FR still attaches via the
604	legacy label; the degraded path is never an error).
605	
606	### Label path (fallback — legacy `milestone_binding: label`)
607	
608	Each FR's frontmatter `milestone: M<N>` maps to the
609	`milestone-<M-token>` label (e.g. `milestone-M86`), and the milestone-attach
610	flow (`/spec-write` § 0b, `/implement` Phase 1 step 0.e) attaches that label
611	to the pushed ticket.
612	
613	**Mapping.** FR `milestone: M<N>` → the `milestone-<M-token>` label. The
614	token is the raw milestone token (`M86`), giving labels like
615	`milestone-M86`. The label is created implicitly the first time it is
616	attached — there is no pre-existing tracker milestone object to look up
617	(this is the `N/A (create-on-write)` missing-milestone handling from
618	`docs/tracker-adapters.md`).
619	
620	**Attach — `editJiraIssue` read-merge-write.** Jira's MCP has no top-level
621	`labels` parameter on the edit path and no append-a-label operation; a
622	naive write would clobber every other label on the issue. So the attach is
623	a **read-merge-write** cycle:
624	
625	1. **Read** — `mcp__atlassian__getJiraIssue(issueIdOrKey=ticket_id)` and
626	   capture the issue's current `labels` array.
627	2. **Merge** — union the existing labels with `milestone-<M-token>`; if the
628	   label is already present this is a no-op set (idempotent).
629	3. **Write** — `mcp__atlassian__editJiraIssue(issueIdOrKey=ticket_id,
630	   additional_fields={ labels: <merged set> })` with the full merged array,
631	   so no pre-existing label is dropped. (There is no top-level `labels`
632	   parameter — labels go through `additional_fields.labels`, the same path
633	   the on-create `default_labels` rule uses; see the MCP tool-names table.)
634	
635	**Read-back verify.** After the write, **re-read** the issue
636	(`getJiraIssue`) and assert the `milestone-<M-token>` label is present in
637	the returned `labels` — the read-back verify confirms the attach landed
638	(the same silent-no-op discipline the metadata writes use). If the label is
639	absent on read-back, surface an NFR-10 canonical-shape warning rather than
640	reporting success.
641	
642	**`default_labels` carve-out (on-create only).** The `### Jira`.default_labels
643	workspace-binding field applies **only on create** (`createJiraIssue`),
644	per the workspace-binding rule documented under `upsert_ticket_metadata`.
645	The milestone-attach read-merge-write runs on the **edit** path and is
646	entirely independent of `default_labels`: it neither reads nor reapplies
647	`default_labels`, and attaching a milestone label never re-triggers the
648	create-time default-labels behaviour. Conversely, a create that seeds
649	`default_labels` does not attach the milestone label — milestone binding is
650	always its own explicit read-merge-write step.
651

# `/spec-write` Tracker Mode Flow

> See `docs/layout-reference.md` — canonical authority on FR file shape (per-FR file path, AC-prefix derivation, `## Acceptance Criteria` section).

Detailed tracker-mode procedures for `/spec-write`. Pointed at from
`skills/spec-write/SKILL.md` step 0 to keep the skill under NFR-1.

In `mode: none`, this document is unused.

## Tracker ID Assignment Order

**Rule:** create the tracker ticket **first**, read the returned ID, substitute the placeholder globally, **then** write the FR file. **Never guess** the next sequential tracker number.

The order is load-bearing. Trackers skip cancelled numbers, renumber across workspace renames, and allocate IDs atomically on ticket creation — an implementer's guess ("`<TKR>-NN` was last, so the next is `<TKR>-NN+1`") can be wrong silently, and the misalignment ships into every downstream artifact (AC prefixes, filename, plan-file row, every prose cross-reference).

### Concrete flow

1. **Draft with placeholder.** Use `<tracker-id>` (or adapter-specific rendering — `STE-<N>` for Linear, `PROJ-<N>` for Jira) throughout the draft:
   - AC lines: `AC-<tracker-id>.1`, `AC-<tracker-id>.2`, …
   - Filename: `<tracker-id>.md`
   - Plan-file table row: `| <tracker-id> | Title | <tracker>:<tracker-id> |`
   - Prose cross-references: `"closes <tracker-id>"`, `"supersedes <tracker-id>"`
2. **Create the tracker ticket.** Call `Provider.sync(spec)` → `upsertTicketMetadata(null, …)`. **Workspace binding.** Before invoking, call `readWorkspaceBinding(claudeMdPath, "linear" | "jira")` from `adapters/_shared/src/workspace_binding.ts` and pass `team` + `project` + `defaultLabels` into the call so the new ticket lands on the correct project board with the configured labels. Linear adapter rejects creates that lack `project` per the silent-landing trap; Jira adapter rejects creates that lack `project` per the Jira API requirement. **Labels** are optional and forwarded only when `defaultLabels` is populated (Linear → `save_issue.labels`; Jira → `createJiraIssue.additional_fields.labels`). The tracker allocator returns the real ID (e.g., `<TKR>-NN`).
3. **Substitute globally.** Replace every `<tracker-id>` with the returned ID in one pass.
4. **Write the FR file.** Only after substitution completes — the file on disk never contains a placeholder.

### Worked example

Draft AC line: `AC-<tracker-id>.1: releaseLock asserts pre-state in_progress`

Linear assigns the next free ID (let's call it `<TKR>-NN`) on save.

Final AC line in file: `AC-<TKR>-NN.1: releaseLock asserts pre-state in_progress`
Filename: `specs/frs/<TKR>-NN.md`
Plan row: `| <TKR>-NN | Hide full 26-char ULIDs | linear:<TKR>-NN |`

### Mode: none exemption

Mode: none projects mint the short-ULID tail locally (collision-proof by Crockford Base32 randomness + scan). No tracker allocator, no race. The placeholder rule is tracker-mode only.

## Post-save behavior (tracker mode)

After each AC-list save in `specs/frs/<tracker-id>.md`'s
`## Acceptance Criteria` section:

1. Resolve the ticket-id for the edited FR directly from the filename
   (`<tracker-id>.md`) — the filename IS the binding, no separate
   traceability matrix is consulted. If the FR is brand-new and the
   filename still carries the `<tracker-id>` placeholder, prompt the
   user for a fresh `upsert_ticket_metadata(null, ...)` invocation that
   creates the ticket and substitutes the returned ID per the
   placeholder rule above.
2. Run ticket-binding confirmation per `docs/ticket-binding.md`.
3. Call `pull_acs(ticket_id)` — fresh fetch, just like `/implement` does.
4. Classify the local AC list vs the tracker AC list via the bidirectional
   diff classifier (`adapters/_shared/src/classify_diff.ts`). Full procedure
   in `docs/ac-sync.md`.
5. If any AC is non-`identical`, surface the Schema K diff and run the
   per-AC prompt loop. **Cancel aborts the save** — local changes revert
   to the in-memory draft state (the user re-decides).
6. On resolution (including `all identical` fast path), call
   `upsert_ticket_metadata(ticket_id, title, <rebuilt description>)` to
   push the converged state to the tracker.
   `git log` captures the sync event via the commit; no separate audit
   trail is written.

`/spec-write` on a brand-new FR (no ticket bound yet) skips steps 1–5 and
goes straight to `upsert_ticket_metadata(null, title, description)` to
mint a new ticket; the returned ID becomes the FR filename
(`specs/frs/<tracker-id>.md`) — the filename IS the binding (no
separate traceability matrix is maintained).

## Cancel semantics

- **During diff/resolve cancel (step 5):** local draft stays in memory;
  tracker untouched. User can retry or abandon.
- **During mint-new cancel:** no `upsert_ticket_metadata` call; no FR
  file is written to disk (the draft stays in memory — cancel here means
  "don't push to tracker, don't land the file yet").

## Orphan listing

`/spec-write` § 0.5 never improvises the tracker-orphan list. Fetch the
container with the adapter's `list_active_frs` read (see `adapters/jira.md`
and `adapters/linear.md`), save every page verbatim as a JSON file, then run:

```bash
bun run ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/adapters/_shared/src/container_ownership.ts list <projectRoot> <page.json>...
```

Page fields the listing needs:

- **Jira** (`searchJiraIssuesUsingJql`, paginated to `isLast: true`): `key`,
  `summary`, `issuetype`, `labels`, `description`, `creator`, `project`.
- **Linear** (`list_issues`, cursor followed to `hasNextPage: false`):
  `id` / `identifier`, `title`, `labels`, `description`, `createdBy`,
  `project`, `team`.

A repository that declares a shared tracker refuses a page whose ticket lacks
`labels` or `description`, naming the file or the key; a missing or non-JSON
page file refuses too, and nothing is listed from a page that failed to parse.

The listing prints one table row per unbound ticket — `Key`, `Class`, `Owner`
(the creator), `Toolkit-written` (the `Source: specs/frs/<key>.md` back-link,
reported only; it is not ownership evidence) and `Title` — then a `summary:`
line counting every class, the excluded ones included. Classes: `ours` (carries
this repository's `repo_tag`), `unowned` (no owner label — hand-filed, or a
client too old to tag), `sibling` (another repository's label) and `container`
(a Jira Epic or any hierarchy level above the FR). `sibling` and `container`
tickets are counted and never offered. Each offerable ticket gets one line
carrying the two option labels to show verbatim:

```
options: Import <KEY> | Skip <KEY>
```

On an explicit `Import <KEY>` answer, record consent before the import:

```bash
bun run ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/adapters/_shared/src/container_ownership.ts consent <projectRoot> <KEY> <page.json>...
```

`consent` re-classifies the same pages and, in a shared repository, writes an
`import` receipt for an `ours` or `unowned` key only; it refuses a `sibling`,
`container` or unlisted key with nothing written. An undeclared repository
writes no receipt.

Then hand the same saved pages to the import as its ownership context,
`importFromTracker(trackerKey, trackerId, provider, specsDir, promptMilestone,
{ projectRoot, pages })`. With the pages, a `sibling` or `container` key
refuses before any write. Importing an `unowned` ticket claims it: the sync
adds this repository's tag to the labels the page shows, so the sibling's next
listing classifies it `sibling`. In a shared repository, a page that lacks the
ticket or its `labels` refuses rather than risk a label set that drops a
label. Where the tag write never lands, probe #49's `bound-ticket-untagged`
row names the ticket.

## MCP call budget (NFR-8)

Per FR save: at most **1** MCP call (`upsert_ticket_metadata`, ≤ 1 per
spec). The additional `pull_acs` in step 3 is shared with the same skill's
pre-flight work and counts toward the 2-call `/implement` budget in
sessions where `/spec-write` chains into `/implement`.
